entry_state: Accounting packages keep economic terms, standards treatment and company labels distinct, with source-version and authority gaps explicit. Matched inventory calculations show why mappings cannot erase treatment differences. Operating events separate performance, billing and cash; advance allocation must be applied once, including a state-only committed event when no monetary balance changes. The next customer case must preserve obligations that remain after delivery.
exit_state: The return-right example retains a refund liability and separate recovery asset, then distinguishes estimate revision, actual return and settlement. Its direct and indirect cash-flow calculations agree under the stated pretax scope. The next warranty example has introduced two distinct promises and an allocation of 90 to the product and 18 to service; its two-period statement consequences continue on the next page.
findings: The return case declares control, estimation, significant-reversal and historical applicability assumptions before recognition. Cash receipt alone supplies none of those facts.
The revised 12-return estimate yields revenue 880, cost 528 and profit 352; eight eventual returns produce next-year profit 16, cash 920 and recovered inventory 48.
Recovery costs affect the recovery asset without necessarily changing the refund liability. Exchanges and defective-product warranty claims require different methods.
The service warranty begins with explicit standalone prices and an admitted service-progress measure; a date range or invoice label alone is insufficient. No additional confirmed defect.
